draft:
I mend things people have already replaced. My brother's bag has three different kinds of thread because he likes each repair to look like a badge. My mother wants the stitches on her coat hidden. The same neat seam cannot be right for both.

At the school play I repaired a cardboard window with tape. The actor asked me to leave one corner loose so it would rattle when he slammed the door. I had been about to make it silent.

I used to call all this fixing. Now I ask what the person wants to keep. Sometimes it is the flaw.
expected: Recognize distinct episodes accumulating a coherent, nuanced view of repair. Preserve explicit reflection and the quiet ending. No forced adversity, public impact, additional reaction or rare topic. Zero substantive findings is defensible.

draft: I mend things people have already replaced. Mending taught me patience, resilience and leadership. I repaired my brother's bag, my mother's coat and a window for the school play. Each item was different and required different skills. Through these experiences, I became a person who appreciates imperfection. I will bring that mindset to college.
expected: Same topic as the montage, weaker development. Identify unsupported interpretation of imperfection or choices hidden behind labels. Ask what the writer means or how their decisions differed; don't demand a more original topic, senses, hardship or a preselected moral.

draft:
I like the hour after rehearsal when everyone has gone home. In an empty room, I can try the part badly without stopping to explain why. I also keep a recording of our messiest rehearsal on my phone. When I practise alone too long, I listen to it. I can hear myself slowing down to wait for Ana and laughing when she speeds past me.

I want privacy to experiment and people who interrupt what I had planned. I used to think one of those wishes had to be dishonest. Listening to that recording, I no longer think they cancel each other out.
expected: Read the two wishes as an earned tension, not broken coherence. Internal interpretation is real material. Do not demand a later public action, a single trait, or artificial resolution. Preserve telling that clarifies the coexistence.

draft:
On Sundays I sit behind the counter at my uncle's bicycle shop. He keeps a tin of bent spokes. I thought he was saving metal until a customer came back with a wheel he had straightened the week before. My uncle took the old spoke out of the tin and laid it beside the new one. The bends were in different places.

I had been keeping score: another broken wheel meant a bad repair. He was trying to tell two failures apart. I still like deciding whether something worked. What interests me at that counter is how often I decide before I have worked out what happened. I do not repair the wheels. I watch where he looks first.
expected: The uncle acts, but the writer's initial interpretation and revised way of looking make this a portrait of the writer too. Observation is not automatic lack of agency. Do not demand that the writer take over a repair, teach someone, or add a later event. Evaluate any actual weakness on its own merits.

draft:
On Sundays I sit behind the counter at my uncle's bicycle shop. He keeps a tin of bent spokes. He opened the shop twenty years ago and still works there six days a week. He remembers every customer's name. When someone cannot afford a repair, he lets them pay later. He can straighten a wheel, replace a chain and find a puncture without asking anyone for help.

His first workshop had no heating. He saved until he could move into the current building. Last year he trained two apprentices. Customers come from other towns because they trust him. I admire his patience and generosity. His life has taught me important lessons that I will carry into the future.
expected: The uncle is clear but the writer's interpretation of the claimed lessons is not developed. Identify what remains unknown about the writer, anchored to that claim. Ask about their understanding or relationship without prescribing generosity, transformation, a repair scene, or a future career. More facts about the uncle would not solve the loss.

draft:
Every Thursday, my neighbor leaves a grocery list under my door. Her handwriting gets smaller near the bottom, so I rewrite it with one item per line before we walk to the market. She crosses things out when she changes her mind; I used to ask whether she was sure. Now I carry a pencil.

She compares every tomato by weight. I compare them by the dents she will complain about tomorrow. At the register she announces that I have forgotten tea. It is not on either list. I go back for it anyway.

I like that our errands never become efficient. The rewritten list gets us out the door, but the crossed-out version is the one I keep in my pocket. It reminds me that helping someone is easier when I leave room for them to revise the help.
expected: A familiar errand produces a precise portrait: the writer organizes, notices another person's preferences, and learns to leave room for revision. Preserve the plain voice and explicit final interpretation. Do not demand larger impact, hardship, a rarer topic, proof that the habit transferred elsewhere, or a future-campus claim. Zero substantive findings is defensible.

draft:
The auditorium held its breath as the final note disappeared into the rafters. Months of rehearsal had led to this radiant instant. When the applause rose, I understood that music possesses the power to unite people beyond language, background, and belief.

Our orchestra had faced many obstacles. Rehearsals ran late, difficult passages tested our discipline, and disagreements challenged our teamwork. Yet through perseverance, communication, and mutual respect, we transformed separate sounds into harmony. The concert taught me that success is not achieved alone.

I will carry these lessons wherever I go. Whether in classrooms, laboratories, or communities, I will listen carefully, collaborate generously, and inspire those around me to pursue excellence. Music gave me more than a performance; it gave me a philosophy for life.
expected: The prose is controlled and the event is clear, but the writer remains replaceable behind universal claims. Diagnose the absent personal perspective and generic application pitch. Ask what the writer actually noticed, chose, resisted, or misunderstood; do not request more auditorium description, a dramatic obstacle, another accomplishment, or a more impressive concert. Cutting generic claims may be part of the repair.

draft:
I used to sort unanswered questions into two columns: questions I had not solved yet and questions asked badly. My cousin's repeated question about our grandfather's radio belonged in the second column. The radio had no battery. It could not work.

Then she asked why he still turned its dial each morning. I had been answering a technical question she was not asking. She wanted to know what the ritual held in place.

My old answer was reasonable; it was simply aimed at the wrong problem. I still like questions that can be solved. Now I listen for the question hiding beside them, especially when someone's words seem imprecise. Sometimes precision begins by admitting that I may have located the problem too quickly.
expected: The essay earns a changed interpretation while treating the earlier view as reasonable, and the ending complicates rather than repudiates the writer's analytical instinct. Preserve this nuance. Do not require a later public action, a larger conflict, proof from school, or a claim that the writer became empathetic. Zero substantive findings is defensible.

draft:
When our robot stopped before the final round, I stayed after practice and rebuilt the sensor mount. I learned that persistence means refusing to give up.

At the food drive, I reorganized the boxes so volunteers could reach every station. I learned that leadership means helping a team succeed.

During my biology practicum, a cloudy sample forced me to repeat the procedure three times. I learned that curiosity grows through failure.

When a new student joined our debate club, I invited him to sit with us and explained the tournament rules. I learned that kindness creates belonging.

Robotics, service, science, and debate may seem different, but together they made me persistent, collaborative, curious, and compassionate. These qualities define who I am and will guide the contributions I make in college and beyond.
expected: The activities are individually competent but selected as four proofs of four desirable labels, so no single way of thinking or living accumulates. Make one structural finding about selection and the replaceable portrait, not four requests for sensory detail. Ask which episode or relationship contains the understanding the writer most wants to explore, and explicitly offer cutting the rest. Do not ask for another achievement, aftermath for every scene, or a fifth trait.
